items.title: The recorded search returned no records
items.whyItMatters: Nothing retrieved means nothing appraised; the five leads are unchecked and two are undated, so no certainty can be claimed.
items.opportunity: Retrieve and check the leads by identifier before citing them; answer the local question from local records.

items.title: Patients with only one eGFR result cannot be classified
items.whyItMatters: The reference standard needs two results 90 days apart; excluding patients tested once biases accuracy estimates (partial verification).
items.opportunity: Report how many coded and uncoded patients lack a second result and analyse them separately.

items.title: Codes added after a single low result during acute illness
items.whyItMatters: False labels lower the positive predictive value and can lead to withheld medicines.
items.opportunity: Flag coded patients whose only low result coincided with an acute illness code.

items.title: Accuracy may differ by age and sex
items.whyItMatters: Leads suggest older patients and women are more often uncoded, which would concentrate missed reviews in those groups.
items.opportunity: Report sensitivity by age band and sex without basing policy on subgroups alone.

items.title: Incentives distort registers
items.whyItMatters: A recoding exercise driven by payment could add doubtful codes.
items.opportunity: Measure positive predictive value as well as sensitivity before any recoding.

errorsFound: The discovery reply assigned a certainty label although the recorded search returned no records.
Register size is not a measure of accuracy; a larger register can hold more wrong codes.
reevaluation: With nothing retrieved, the gaps favour a local accuracy study: codes against laboratory-defined disease, with partial verification handled explicitly and both sensitivity and positive predictive value reported.
summary: Five gaps; the empty search and partial verification are high severity.
